newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-RUSSIA'S ZELENSKAYA WINS WOMEN'S ALPINE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-RUSSIA'S ZELENSKAYA WINS WOMEN'S ALPINE.

text.p: Varvara Zelenskaya of Russia won a World Cup women's downhill race on Friday with a time of one minute 35.59 seconds.
Hilary Lindh of the United States captured second place with a time of 1:36.01, followed by Carole Montillet of France at 1:36.03.
Zelenskaya navigated a course made bumpy and hard by overnight cold after a mild Thursday to her second World Cup victory of the season and third of her career.
"When the snow is harder it is harder to keep speed," she told a news conference.

Lindh, who won the World Championship in Sestriere, Italy, earlier this month, told reporters: "Obviously, winning the World Championships really helped my confidence. It was very bumpy and I just tried not to get thrown around too much."
